entries.title: High-intensity interval versus moderate continuous training on glycemic control in type 2 diabetes: a randomized controlled trial
entries.summary: In this randomized controlled trial, adults with type 2 diabetes performed high-intensity interval training or moderate continuous training for 12 weeks. HbA1c and glycemic control improved more with high-intensity interval training than with moderate continuous training.

entries.title: High-intensity interval training and endothelial function in adults with type 2 diabetes
entries.summary: Adults with type 2 diabetes underwent high-intensity interval training for 8 weeks. Endothelial function, measured by flow-mediated dilation, was the primary endpoint; glycemic markers were not assessed.

entries.title: Sprint interval training improves HbA1c and insulin sensitivity in adults with type 2 diabetes: a randomized trial
entries.summary: Preprint version of a randomized trial in which adults with type 2 diabetes were assigned to sprint interval training or moderate continuous training for 10 weeks; HbA1c and insulin sensitivity were the main outcomes.
